# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop Drawing
*Draw a single continuous loop through the grid.*

- **Masyu** – Loop constrained by black/white circle turning rules
- **Slitherlink** – Loop drawn on dot grid, constrained by number clues on cells
- **Mid-loop** – Loop where black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directional loop with wind constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop alternating between moon/sun symbols across rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop constrained by white circles (straight or turn) and avoiding black circles within bold-line areas
- **Suraromu** – Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in order
- **Yajilin** – Loop with black cells placed according to arrow/number clues

### B. Path/Connection Drawing
*Draw paths or connections (not necessarily a single loop).*

- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect islands with bridges (1 or 2) matching island numbers; all connected
- **Pencils** – Draw lines from pencil tips through cells, constrained by pencil length
- **Evolomino** – Place growing blocks along arrows

### C. Cell Shading / Painting
*Determine which cells to shade black (or leave white).*

#### C1. Shading with number clues about adjacent/nearby black cells
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs; numbers on black squares indicate adjacent bulb count
- **Kurotto** – Numbers in circles = sum of sizes of contiguous black groups touching the circle
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers = count of visible white cells in four directions
- **Nurikabe** – Numbers define white island sizes; black cells form one connected wall, no 2×2
- **Nurimisaki** – Circle cells are white promontories; numbers indicate white line length
- **Usowan** – Numbers show adjacent black cell count, but one number per room is wrong
- **Norinori** – Each bold-line region gets exactly two black cells forming a domino
- **Nuritwin** – Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks

#### C2. Shading forming specific shapes
- **Choco Banana** – Black groups must be rectangles/squares; white groups must not be rectangles/squares; numbers indicate group size
- **LITS** – Place one tetromino per region; same-shape tetrominoes can't touch; connected; no 2×2
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares
- **Tilepaint** – Color entire tiles (bold-line regions) to match row/column black-cell counts

#### C3. Shading with connectivity/separation constraints
- **Heyawake** – Numbers indicate black cells per room; no two black cells adjacent; white cells connected; white can't span 3+ rooms in a line
- **Sto-stone** – Black cells per room given by number; black cells don't connect across rooms; when "dropped" they fill bottom half

### D. Cell Filling (Numbers or Symbols)

#### D1. Number placement with uniqueness constraints
- **Sudoku** – Fill 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 blocks without repetition
- **Hitori** – Black out duplicate numbers so no repeats remain in rows/columns; black cells non-adjacent; white cells connected

#### D2. Number placement with region/proximity constraints
- **Fillomino** – Fill numbers; groups of same number have size equal to that number; same-sized groups can't touch
- **Ripple Effect** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; duplicate numbers in a line must be spaced apart by at least the number's value
- **Makaro** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; arrows indicate which neighbor has the largest value; same numbers can't be adjacent across rooms
- **Nansuke** – Place given multi-digit numbers into a crossword-style grid

#### D3. Symbol placement
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference; runs limited to 2 vertically for — and 2 horizontally for |

### E. Grid Division / Partitioning
*Divide the grid into regions satisfying constraints.*

- **Shikaku** – Divide into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** – Divide into pentominoes; numbers indicate surrounding border-line count
- **Double Choco** – Divide so each block has matching white and gray sub-regions of identical shape
- **Sashigane** – Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark ends

### F. Object Movement / Placement
*Move or place objects within the grid.*

- **Satogaeri** – Move circles so each country has exactly one; numbers indicate distance moved; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** – Move circles into gray areas via straight arrows; numbers in gray areas equal sum of entering circles
- **Hebi** – Place snakes (1–5 sequences) with adjacency and line-of-sight constraints

### G. Hybrid: Shading + Additional Structure
- **Chained Block** – Shade cells into blocks; numbers indicate block size; blocks chain diagonally; no duplicate shapes per chain
- **Nurimeizu** – Shade entire rooms to create a maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles not

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanism

### A. Clue Type

| Clue Mechanism | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Adjacent count** (how many special cells neighbor a clue) | Akari, Shakashaka, Usowan, Slitherlink, Five Cells |
| **Directional/visibility count** (count along a line of sight) | Kurodoko, Yajilin, Hebi, Pencils, Tilepaint |
| **Region total/count** (number of marked cells in a bold-line region) | Heyawake, Nuritwin, Norinori, Sto-stone, Choco Banana |
| **Group size** (number = size of the connected group containing the clue) | Fillomino, Chained Block, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Shikaku |
| **Sum of adjacent groups** | Kurotto |
| **Sequence/order** | Makaro (arrows for max neighbor), Suraromu (gate crossing order), Ripple Effect (spacing rule) |
| **Movement distance** | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| **Turning/direction rules at clue cells** | Masyu (black/white circles), Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Nagareru |

### B. Global Structural Constraints

| Constraint | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Single loop** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| **All white cells connected** | Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Usowan, Nurimeizu |
| **All shaded cells connected** | LITS, Nuritwin |
| **No 2×2 black square** | Nurikabe, LITS, Sto-stone, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki |
| **No 2×2 same-color square** | Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu |
| **Black cells non-adjacent** | Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Usowan, Yajilin |
| **No same-size/shape groups touching** | Fillomino, LITS, Chained Block |
| **Complete grid coverage** (every cell assigned) | Sudoku, Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Juosan, Nansuke, Shikaku, Five Cells, Sashigane |
| **Gravity/dropping** | Sto-stone |
| **Deception** (one clue per region is wrong) | Usowan |

---

## III. By Grid Element Used

### A. Plain Grid (cells only)
Sudoku, Fillomino, Hitori, Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Choco Banana, Juosan, Tilepaint, Nansuke

### B. Grid with Bold-Line Regions
Heyawake, Norinori, LITS, Double Choco, Five Cells, Shikaku, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Sto-stone, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu, Sashigane, Satogaeri, Usowan, Chained Block, Suraromu

### C. Grid with Circles/Symbols in Cells
Masyu (black/white circles), Mid-loop (black circles), Nurimisaki (numbered circles), Kurotto (numbered circles), Akari (numbered black squares), Hashiwokakero (numbered circles/islands), Hebi (numbered/arrowed black squares), Yosenabe (numbered circles), Satogaeri (numbered circles)

### D. Dot Grid (lines on edges)
Slitherlink

### E. Grid with Arrows/Directional Elements
Yajilin, Makaro, Nagareru, Evolomino, Pencils, Sashigane, Hebi

---

## IV. Summary Tree

```
Grid-Based Logic Puzzles
├── Loop/Path Construction
│   ├── Single Loop
│   │   ├── Edge-based: Slitherlink
│   │   └── Cell-center-based
│   │       ├── Circle constraints: Masyu, Mid-loop, Dotchi-Loop
│   │       ├── Room constraints: Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu
│   │       ├── Direction constraints: Nagareru
│   │       └── Hybrid (loop + shading): Yajilin
│   └── Paths/Connections
│       ├── Pair connections: Numberlink
│       ├── Bridge networks: Hashiwokakero
│       └── Directed paths: Pencils, Evolomino
│
├── Cell Determination
│   ├── Shading (black/white)
│   │   ├── Number-adjacent clues: Akari, Kurotto, Kurodoko, Usowan
│   │   ├── Region-count clues: Heyawake, Norinori, Nuritwin, Sto-stone
│   │   ├── Island/wall structure: Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu
│   │   ├── Shape constraints: Choco Banana, LITS, Shakashaka, Tilepaint
│   │   └── Block structure: Chained Block
│   │
│   ├── Number/Symbol Filling
│   │   ├── Latin-square family: Sudoku, Hitori
│   │   ├── Region-sequential: Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro
│   │   ├── Crossword-style: Nansuke
│   │   ├── Symbol placement: Juosan
│   │   └── Sequence placement: Hebi
│   │
│   └── Grid Partitioning
│       ├── Into rectangles: Shikaku
│       ├── Into fixed-size regions: Five Cells
│       ├── Into matching-pair regions: Double Choco
│       └── Into L-shapes: Sashigane
│
└── Object Movement
    ├── Circle movement into regions: Yosenabe
    └── Circle repositioning within countries: Satogaeri
```
